subject: SLA redlines: availability bands, credits & maintenance windows (Order Form)
messages:
From: Tom Keller <tkeller@aventis.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form SLA redlines and availability targets

Marissa,

Thanks for the draft Order Form. Our legal and SRE teams reviewed the SLA and pushed back on a few items — attached is a tracked redline with our asks. High level:

- Availability: Aventis needs a minimum of 99.9% availability per calendar month for the API endpoint used by our production customers.
- Maintenance: we want a stricter maintenance carveout — scheduled maintenance must be notified 14 days in advance and limited to 4 hours/month per region.
- Credits: if availability falls below 99.9% in a month, we expect a prorated credit that scales with downtime (we attached a suggested table).
- Response times: P1 response within 1 hour and P2 within 4 hours during business hours; escalations to your on-call if unresolved in 3 hours.

Our procurement team also asked for an explicit exceptions list for emergency maintenance and security patches (they're okay with limited weekend emergency maintenance but want scope defined).

Attached: Aventis_SLA_Redlines_v1.docx (tracked changes).

Can we get Redwood's counterproposal by EOD Monday? We are trying to close the Order Form this week to align billing with our Q4 plan.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Keller
Director, Platform Engineering
Aventis Systems

Subject: Re: Order Form SLA redlines and availability targets

Tom —

Appreciate the quick read and the redlines. Good summary; we've reviewed with Product and Ops and have a short counterproposal below. I'll attach a redline/clean pair for legal, but wanted to share the operational tradeoffs up front so we can iterate quickly.

Counterproposal (high level):
- Availability banding: we can commit to 99.95% availability (API regionally measured) on our production endpoints for the primary service SKU. For clarity: availability measured as successful request rate excluding traffic we explicitly route to fallback variants.
- Credits: we propose a staircase credit table instead of linear prorating — 99.95–99.90 => 5% of monthly invoice; 99.90–99.50 => 15%; <99.50 => 40%. We believe this aligns incentives and caps exposure for both sides.
- Maintenance windows: we are comfortable with scheduled maintenance notices at least 7 days in advance and propose a standard monthly maintenance budget of up to 6 hours/month per region. For larger planned migrations that exceed 6 hours, we will notify 21 days in advance and offer a rollback plan.
- Emergency/security patches: carveouts for zero-day security patches and mitigations; we will notify within 2 hours post-change and provide a postmortem within 72 hours.
- Response & escalation: P1 acknowledgement within 30 minutes (24/7), P1 remediation SLA target within 4 hours; P2 acknowledgement within 2 hours (business hours). We will publish a named escalation path and on-call contacts in a secure doc.

Operational notes: continuous batching and autoscaling can reduce incident surface; however, guaranteeing sub-1-hour remediation for complex model regressions is not operationally viable without a managed runbook and joint escalation. If Aventis requires a 1-hour remediation closure, we should discuss a dedicated capacity plan (Redwood Dedicated) and a higher committed spend.

I'll attach our redline for legal review (Redwood_SLA_Counterproposal.pdf). Rishi — can you loop in Legal and Agreements to review the attached redline vs their tracked doc and flag any absolute blockers? Karthik — can you confirm the regional measurement definition matches how Ops reports availability?

Tom — if this looks directionally acceptable, let's book 30 minutes Monday to finalize numeric tables and procurement steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole

marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0162

Subject: Re: Order Form SLA redlines and availability targets

Thanks, Marissa — good summary. A few legal/agreements asks to keep the redline process tidy:

1) Separate redlines: please keep MSA redlines and Order Form SLA redlines in separate documents. Legal needs the MSA to remain the source of truth for remedies and limitations; the Order Form should reference the MSA and include the numeric SLA table.

2) Measurement & exclusions: we need specific measurement definitions in the Order Form: regional endpoint list, measurement window (one calendar month), and explicit excluded events (force majeure, customer-caused outages, third-party provider outages, DNS or routing changes initiated by Aventis).

3) Credit calculation: Legal is okay with a staircase credit table but requests a maximum aggregate cap (we recommend cap of two months' credits per 12-month period) and a clause that credits are sole and exclusive remedy for availability claims.

4) Emergency maintenance: define "emergency maintenance" and require Redwood to provide an incident summary and mitigation plan within 72 hours. Legal will keep the 14-day scheduled-maintenance notice ask as negotiable — Ops prefers 7 days.

Action items:
- Marissa: produce redline pair (MSA redline + Order Form clean) and upload to the HubSpot deal and to the shared drive.
- Karthik: confirm regional measurement buckets and provide example metrics (last 90 days) so Aventis can validate.
- Legal: I'll have agreements review the attached counterproposal and return comments by EOD Tuesday.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
